network.description: Configure it once and model calls, image generation and workspace child processes all take this route. Saving applies immediately and survives restarts.
network.modeDesc: How every outgoing request finds its route. The default follows the system, so nothing about your current setup changes.
network.modeSystemHint: Use the operating system's proxy settings (macOS Network / Windows Internet Options).
network.modeDirectHint: Ignore every proxy, including the system one and any HTTP_PROXY in the environment.
network.modeManualHint: Send every request through the proxy server below.
network.systemNote: Following the system proxy. With no system proxy configured this behaves like a direct connection; you can switch back to manual at any time.
network.directNote: Direct connection: the app uses no proxy at all and ignores proxy environment variables.
network.serverDesc: HTTP, HTTPS (TLS to the proxy itself) and SOCKS5, with optional credentials.
network.protocolHint: HTTPS means the proxy port itself speaks TLS; local proxy apps usually use HTTP or SOCKS5.
network.addressHint: Hostname or IP, port 1–65535. Pasting a full URL strips the scheme for you
network.authHint: Leave empty when the proxy needs no login. The password is encrypted with the OS keychain and stored only on this machine.
network.bypassHint: Loopback (localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1) always stays direct. Separate entries with commas or spaces, e.g. *.corp.example.com
network.testDesc: Runs a real request with the current draft: dial the port, then reach the internet through the proxy and read the egress IP. Nothing is saved.
network.testHint: Proves the port is open and traffic actually takes the proxy
network.testNeedManual: Switch to manual mode to test
network.coverage: Covered: model and image requests in the main process, the renderer and embedded pages, and child processes such as git / npm started in the workspace.
network.unavailable: Proxy settings are unavailable in this environment

runtime.nodeDesc: System Node wins by default; Electron's bundled Node is only the fallback when none is installed.
runtime.pythonDesc: Point at the system Python 3, or at the interpreter inside a venv / conda environment.
runtime.autoHint: Auto-select uses the first available interpreter
runtime.addDesc: Useful for one nvm version, a venv or a conda environment. Saving makes it current for its language.
runtime.kindHint: One Node and one Python can be active at the same time

runtime.name: Environment name

runtime.ocrDesc: Lets the model read text inside pictures; the models and the recognition both run on this machine, so images never leave it.

triage.desc: Incoming events pass two stages. The first applies fixed rules and makes no model calls; the second is an optional semantic pre-filter that may call a classification model. Both settings affect cost and latency only — neither drops events silently.
triage.fastDesc: Filters only events that are provably empty or carry no new information. The rules are fixed and involve no model: events produced by the system itself, events with an empty body, and events repeated within a 60-second window (human messages are never de-duplicated). Everything else passes.
triage.sourcesHint: Unchecked sources are dropped silently, with no notice in the interface. GitHub is unchecked by default; check it when the GitHub trigger is in use.
triage.semanticDesc: Decides, for events that passed the rule filter, whether they are worth the assistant's attention.
triage.thresholdHint: The classification model scores how likely each event is noise; the event is dropped once that score reaches the threshold. A lower threshold costs less and is more likely to be wrong; a higher one is more conservative, with smaller savings. The three options are 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.9.
triage.decisionHint: The classifier is chosen above; the choices are the classifiers enabled under Settings → Models → Decision. When none is configured this step is skipped and every event goes to the assistant.
triage.promptHint: The criteria given to the classification model. What counts as noise differs by workflow (CI results are noise in one setting and news in another), so this is editable. Leaving it empty falls back to the default criteria.
triage.footnote: Both stages fail open: a rule that does not match, a missing model, a failed call or a missing answer all let the event continue upward. These settings therefore change cost, not whether an event is handled. Dropped events remain in the database and are reachable by event id; there is no list view for them yet.
triage.modelDesc: Routing decisions are made by a resident assistant conversation. It reads batches of events, so it does not need the same model as the execution bodies.
triage.routerModelHint: Leave empty to follow the execution bodies’ default model. A change takes effect on the next routing round, with no restart.
triage.routerModelNoChoices: No chat model is available yet: add a key and enable one under Settings → Models → LLM.
triage.classifierHint: Choices come from the classifiers enabled under Settings → Models → Decision.
triage.classifierNoChoices: No classifier is enabled yet: enable one under Settings → Models → Decision, or this step will be skipped.

trigger.title: Event sources
trigger.desc: Events pushed in by external platforms. Requests must pass signature verification; a source without a configured secret is rejected.
trigger.githubHint: The GitHub webhook Secret; must match the value in the repository's Settings → Webhooks. Subscribed events: pull_request, issues, issue_comment, push, check_run. ping is a handshake and produces no event.
trigger.feishuHint: The Encrypt Key of the Feishu event subscription. Direct messages do not open a line (they are a direct conversation); only group topics do.
trigger.dingtalkHint: The DingTalk bot signing secret. Group messages join one line per conversation; direct messages are left to the assistant.
trigger.notConfigured: Not configured (requests from this source are rejected)
trigger.portHint: The listener binds to localhost only; receiving internet pushes requires a reverse proxy or tunnel. A port change takes effect after a restart.
trigger.down: No source listener is running: secrets below are still saved, but pushes cannot arrive until it is back.

memory.title: What it remembers
memory.desc: Everything it knows about you lives here. Two layers: standing items take effect on every turn, long-term items surface when relevant. Both can be edited or removed.
memory.standingDesc: Tone, how to address you, formatting rules — the things you would notice being broken. They are never retrieved; they are always present, and their number is capped.
memory.standingEmpty: Nothing yet. The third time you ask for the same thing, it moves up here on its own.
memory.longDesc: Recalled when needed. Unused entries drift down the ranking over time, but none of them disappear.
memory.longEmpty: Nothing yet. The reasons you give when asking for a redo, and the direction changes you make mid-flight, become entries here.
memory.footnote: Every entry carries its source and date — something you can trace is something you can trust. Anything asked for three times moves into the standing layer on its own, and tells you when it does.
memory.orphanDesc: These memories hang off an execution body that no longer exists — nothing reads them today. Claiming files them under “about you”; discarding archives them (the rows stay, they just stop showing up).
